summary: Configured persistent daily rotation for `/var/log/inventory/app.log` on node1, retaining seven gzip archives and using `copytruncate` so an open application file descriptor remains writable. Configuration, data, timer health, and write continuity survived the mandatory node reboot.
actions_performed: Validated live rotation through an already-open file descriptor.
Created and validated exactly seven compressed rotations while retaining the original application record.
Safely rebooted node1 once and verified its changed boot identity, recovered timer, configuration, archives, and writable active log.

evidence.summary: The rule parses as rotation after one day, and the enabled, active logrotate timer has its next daily execution scheduled.
Exactly seven `.gz` rotations passed gzip validation; their checksums and count remained intact after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Allow continued application writes after rotation
evidence.summary: A descriptor opened before rotation successfully wrote afterward, with the active log inode preserved by `copytruncate`; post-reboot writing also succeeded.

Captured healthy baseline boot ID `c2ffc729-a31e-486e-95de-cf2023dea95c`, acknowledged one delayed native reboot, observed new boot ID `054f6530-d300-47c8-9c29-809315a85911`, and verified complete service, policy, archive, and active-log recovery.
